name: North Korea
summary_text: North Korea is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Same-sex conduct is not named in the Criminal Code — but Article 193 prohibits “decadent culture,” and broad provisions on obscene activities give authorities unlimited discretion; reported incidents of criminalisation and even execution for homosexuality exist. The concept of gender identity simply does not exist in public life (BBC Korea: sexual minorities are “denied as a concept”). Tourists are under constant escort and surveillance; any nonconforming presentation or discovered digital material risks detention in the world's most totalitarian system.

sources.title: Democratic People's Republic of Korea | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): no laws appear to penalise consensual same-sex acts in the 1950/2009 Criminal Code, but Article 193 prohibits 'decadent culture' (including sexual video recordings) and Article 262 prohibits collective 'obscene activities'; the state denied the existence of same-sex activity in 2014; an unconfirmed 2011 report claimed execution of a lesbian couple; no freedom of assembly.

sources.title: LGBT Rights in North Korea: Legal Status and Reality - LegalClarity
sources.claim_summary: LegalClarity overview (May 2026): North Korea has no law explicitly criminalising same-sex activity, but broad provisions on 'decadent culture' and 'obscene activities' give authorities wide discretion; the government publicly denies LGBT people exist; defectors describe deeply repressive reality.

sources.title: '북한에도 동성애가 있을까?' 개념조차 없이 부정당하는 북한 성소수자, 인권 침해로 봐야 할까 - BBC News 코리아
sources.claim_summary: BBC Korean (Oct 2024, in Korean): 'Does same-sex love exist in North Korea?' - feature on the near-total erasure of North Korean sexual minorities; interviews with defector writer Jang Young-jin; notes new laws (Pyongyang Cultural Language Protection Act, Youth Education Guarantee Law, Rejection of Reactionary Thought and Culture Law) further tightening control; the state does not even acknowledge the concept.

US State Department 2022 Human Rights Report for North Korea: official assessment - the totalitarian regime's pervasive abuses; the report notes no specific law criminalising same-sex conduct but the regime's total control leaves no space for LGBT life.

US State Department 2020 Human Rights Report for North Korea: official assessment - no reliable information on LGBT persons; the regime's repression of all civil society is the dominant human-rights reality.

sources.title: ‘I could not even dream’: Life as a gay North Korea | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Apr 2017): 'I could not even dream: Life as a gay North Korean' — a defector's account of homosexuality's place in North Korean society and its punishment.

KCNA commentary (April 2014): the North Korean state news agency's attack on Michael Kirby, chair of the UN Commission of Inquiry - calling him 'a disgusting old lecher with a 40-odd-year-long career of homosexuality' and claiming homosexuality 'can never be found in the DPRK boasting of sound mentality and good morals' - an official statement of the regime's homophobia.
